collection_metadata.locality: Pitchandikulam Forest, Auroville, Tamil Nadu, India

stem_bark.text: The bark of Cordia myxa is pale brown-coloured with vertical furrows.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Cordia myxa is pale brown-coloured with vertical furrows.

seed.text: The seed of Cordia myxa is enclosed into an ellipsoid and compressed stone. This stone is light brown-coloured and contains 1 seed.
seed.text_html: The seed of Cordia myxa is enclosed into an ellipsoid and compressed stone. This stone is light brown-coloured and contains 1 seed.

fruit.text: The fruit of Cordia myxa is a subglobose drupe . It is about 1.5-2 cm in diameter, pinkish-coloured when ripe. The drupe is seated in a cup-shaped enlarged calyx. Each fruit contains 1 stone.
fruit.text_html: The fruit of Cordia myxa is a subglobose drupe. It is about 1.5-2 cm in diameter, pinkish-coloured when ripe. The drupe is seated in a cup-shaped enlarged calyx. Each fruit contains 1 stone.

leaf.text: The leaves of Cordia myxa grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged). The leaf is simple, dark green-coloured above and paler beneath. The leaf is coriaceous and glabrous on both sides (some minute hairs on the midrib beneath). The leaves have a 2.5-3 cm long petiole . The blade of the leaf of Cordia myxa is 8-12 cm long and 7-10 cm wide. The shape of the blade is ovate, the apex is acuminate, the base is cuneate and the margins are sinuate. The venation of the leaf is reticulate with a prominent midrib.

The leaves have a 2.5-3 cm long petiole.

The venation of the leaf is reticulate with a prominent midrib.

habit.text: Cordia myxa is a thornless, medium-sized and decidous tree growing up to 12-15 m high.
habit.text_html: Cordia myxa is a thornless, medium-sized and decidous tree growing up to 12-15 m high.

reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :
    Cordia myxa is monoecious, with unisexual (male or female) flowers on the same individual.
  • Mode of pollination :
    Cordia myxa is pollinated by a wide variety of insects.
  • Seed dispersal :
    The seeds of Cordia myxa are mainly dispersed by frugivorous birds and mammals.

phenology.text: ( This phenology applies to southeastern Indian plains )
phenology.text_html:
• Flowering season : From March to June.
  • Fruiting season : From March to August.
  • Seeding season : From March to August.
  • Leaves falling : During the hot season.

    • (This phenology applies to southeastern Indian plains)

handicrafts.text: The wood of Cordia myxa is moderately hard. It is used for boat building, agricultural implements, posts, beams, furnitures and carving... A fibre is obtained form the bark and used to make cordage and for caulking boats. The leaves and fruits yield a dye . The sticky, mucilaginous pulp of the fruit is used as a glue . Sources : - Dastur, 2006, Useful Plants of India and Pakistan - Useful Tropical Plants Database, Ken Fern, 2014 (http://tropical.theferns.info)

culinary.text: The ripe fruit of Cordia myxa is eaten raw or cooked. The unripe fruits are eaten as a vegetable or pickled. The leaves and young shoots are used as a vegetable. Source : Useful Tropical Plants Database, Ken Fern, 2014 (http://tropical.theferns.info)

reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :
    Cordia myxa is a light demander and fairly drought resistant. It is drought resistant and it will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils but all soils need to be free draining.
    The species is propagated by seeds or by cuttings.
  • Seed treatments :
    24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
